title: Implementing a collaborative program-wide approach to redeveloping assessment in response to generative artificial intelligence (GenAI)
authors: Kelli Nicola‐Richmond; Phillip Dawson; Justin T. Lawson; Pearse Fay; Judi A. Parson; Susie Macfarlane
source_used: Taylor & Francis OA PDF (CC BY-NC-ND) via doi
ft_reason: HE program-wide assessment redesign in response to GenAI; peer reviewed; 2026.
study_design: Qualitative: combined ethnographic and interpretive phenomenological study of a program-wide assessment redesign project
sample: Academic team members (n=4), project leads (n=3), researchers (n=6); 8 project meetings, 3 focus groups, 12 reflective activities; one Australian university (Deakin)

key_findings.finding: Six themes emerged; success of program-wide redesign depended on wide stakeholder participation, openness and curiosity, and protected time for collaboration and peer learning.
Participants saw few options for assuring learning beyond oral and performative assessments, which they judged hard to run with large or online cohorts.
key_findings.location: Results (challenges and resourcing of assessment change)

dimensions.capability_verification: Staff found oral/performative tasks were the main secure options for assuring learning.
dimensions.scalability: Oral and performative formats were seen as hard to scale to large and online cohorts.
dimensions.workload: Redesign needed dedicated time and resourcing for collaboration.
dimensions.feasibility: Program-wide collaborative redesign was feasible but challenging and resource-dependent.

author_recommendations: Embed time for collaboration and peer learning and involve a range of stakeholders in program-wide redesign.
Use the GenAI moment to improve assessment design more broadly (not tested).
limitations: Single institution, small sample of staff whose assessments changed, data from 2024 only.

quality.note: Clear qualitative design with stated limitations; small single-site sample.

redesign_note: Reports the lived process of implementing a program-wide assessment redesign for GenAI, with enablers and barriers.

title: Pedagogical Implications of ChatGPT on Accounting Assessment in Higher Education
authors: Hannah Wong; Valeriya Avdeev; Sia Nassiripour
venue: International Journal of Economics Business and Management Research
source_used: Journal PDF via doi (ijebmr.com)
ft_reason: HE accounting assessment tasks tested against ChatGPT; academic integrity implications; 2025.
study_design: Descriptive comparison of ChatGPT (GPT-4o) answers versus student scores on course homework and quizzes
sample: One intermediate accounting course section in an online MBA, US public university; 15 homework assignments and 7 quizzes; student cohort size not extracted

key_findings.finding: ChatGPT averaged 87.84% on open-ended homework problems, slightly below the students' 91.73% mean.
ChatGPT averaged 93.33 on unproctored multiple-choice quizzes, above the student mean of 85.86, showing high vulnerability of such tasks.

dimensions.capability_verification: AI scores close to or above students undermine these tasks as evidence of individual capability.
dimensions.integrity_security: Unproctored online quizzes and homework are highly answerable by ChatGPT, creating cheating risk.

author_recommendations: Accounting educators should keep abreast of chatbot advances to keep assessment effective (not tested).
limitations: Single graduate course, prompts entered once without follow-up, so results may not generalise.

quality.note: Simple descriptive test; student n and statistical comparison not reported.

redesign_note: Shows that unproctored online accounting homework and quizzes are largely solvable by GenAI.

title: ChatGPT giving advice on how to cheat in university assignments: how workable are its suggestions?
authors: Dirk H. R. Spennemann; Jessica Maree Biles; Lachlan Brown; Matthew Frank Ireland; Laura Longmore; C. Singh
source_used: Research Square preprint (CC BY), the queue oa_url; may differ from the published ITSE version
ft_reason: HE assignment cheating; tests whether ChatGPT-generated evasion advice would escape markers; 2024 journal version.
study_design: Qualitative content analysis of 30 ChatGPT outputs (role-play prompts) rated by academics for likelihood of escaping detection
sample: 30 iterations of ChatGPT prompts; rated by the authors (academics at Charles Sturt University)

key_findings.finding: Most ChatGPT-suggested strategies for hiding contract cheating had a low chance of escaping detection, but content blending, obscuring plagiarism and distraction techniques had a higher chance of going unnoticed.

dimensions.integrity_security: Some AI-suggested concealment strategies could evade markers, depending on marker vigilance.

author_recommendations: Markers need to stay vigilant to blending and style-masking strategies (not tested).
limitations: Expert judgement of detection likelihood was not tested against real cases.

quality.note: Preprint version used; ratings are author judgement; no explicit limitations section found.

redesign_note: Gives evidence on the limits of marker detection when GenAI is used to plan concealment of outsourced work.

title: Participatory Co-Design and Evaluation of a Novel Approach to Generative AI-Integrated Coursework Assessment in Higher Education
authors: Alex F. Martin; Svitlana Tubaltseva; Anja Harrison; Gideon James Rubin
source_used: Europe PMC full text (PMC12189063) of MDPI CC BY article; MDPI PDF returned 403
ft_reason: Co-designed and evaluated a GenAI-integrated coursework assessment in HE; peer reviewed; 2025.
study_design: Participatory co-design and mixed-methods evaluation with random allocation (compliant vs unrestricted AI use), blinded marking, focus groups and interviews; pre-registered
sample: Cohort of about 30 MSc students at King's College London; 8 students and 4 teaching staff in the evaluation; 20 blogs in the marker identification analysis

key_findings.finding: Blinded markers identified group membership no better than chance (6/14 compliant vs 3/6 unrestricted correct; Fisher's exact p = 1.00), despite some markers feeling confident.
Students found AI did not reduce workload because outputs needed refining; scaffolded AI integration was judged to support critical AI literacy and ethical reflection.

dimensions.integrity_security: Markers could not tell unrestricted AI use from compliant use.
dimensions.appropriate_ai_use: Structured, scaffolded AI use with critical reflection was built into the task.
dimensions.workload: AI did not lower student workload; markers found dual evaluation of AI and student work demanding.
dimensions.feasibility: Co-design toolkit judged feasible and transferable.

author_recommendations: Use participatory co-design with students and staff when building AI-integrated assessments.
Provide workshops, declaration forms and exemplar prompts to support ethical AI use (not tested).
limitations: Single small cohort, students not involved from the start, and feedback taken after the first pilot only.
redesign_note: Implements and evaluates a GenAI-integrated blog assessment and tests whether markers can detect unrestricted AI use.

title: “Broken and Repair” case studies: Developing GenAI-age critical evaluation and creative problem-solving skills in communication education
authors: Triparna Gandhi; Tom Whitford
source_used: Taylor & Francis OA PDF via doi
ft_reason: Peer-reviewed teaching-idea article describing a GenAI-aware case-study assessment in HE; 2026.
sample: Used with about 160 students per year (about 80 per semester) at the University of Melbourne

key_findings.finding: Students diagnose and repair a deliberately flawed professional pitch, which makes reasoning visible and is reported to reduce template-driven answers.

dimensions.authenticity: Uses professionally presented pitches with realistic flaws.
dimensions.appropriate_ai_use: GenAI permitted only for ideation and visualisation during redesign, with a structured usage declaration in the rubric.
dimensions.scalability: Authors state it scales across large cohorts.

author_recommendations: Use deliberately broken cases with bounded GenAI use and graded usage declarations.
limitations: Needs careful scaffolding and subtle errors, and was not formally evaluated.
redesign_note: Describes a specific GenAI-aware assessment design with a graded AI-use declaration.
